name: Animated Line Art
visualIdentity: Animated drawings built from contours, connectors, arrows, and paths with consistent stroke widths, caps, and joins. Objects appear before their relationships; finished structures remain readable. This is a motion technique, distinct from static line art and line boil.
suitableUses: Explicitly suitable for diagrams and contour reveals. It can support technical explainers, process diagrams, educational lessons, product or editorial introductions, and illustrated narratives. Interactive HTML can make responsive SVG diagrams or toggleable annotations. These are suitability suggestions, not required formats.
limitations: Avoid arbitrary tangles, endless redraws, and obscured endpoints or relationships. Omit or adapt chapter transitions when the topic lacks meaningful chapters, a handoff obscures causality, or a cut breaks continuous-shot or loop requirements. Keep explanatory motion readable; do not imply physical production or validated simulation from simulated visuals.
palette: Suggested tokens when no task, brand, or approved source palette exists: background #F9F4E7, foreground #27434A, accent #AA6945. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Preserve supplied colors, role assignments, asset colors, and visual-cue color limits. The accent on the background has contrast 3.971 and is decorative only; use the foreground/background pair for normal text and check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal path length with stroke-dasharray/stroke-dashoffset or DrawSVGPlugin; stage objects before connections, nodes, and arrows in explanatory order. Preserve continuous endpoints and allow reading holds. For video, derive all states from seekable composition time; avoid autonomous loops and verify backward and direct seeks. For HTML, finite scroll progress may scrub chapter handoffs or story steps, with coherent reverse states, accessible reading order, keyboard/touch support, and reduced-motion or static states. Hover and pointer behavior is for interactive delivery only.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic, audience, and explicit audio requirements. State assumptions when inputs are absent; do not invent available assets. Synchronize through the composition pipeline and check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Use task-provided or authorized assets and exact copy; load local fonts and assets before animation. SVG is the primary scalable drawing option. Optional tools can author diagrams, graph layouts, vector paths, or procedural contours; they require deliberate styling and cached, deterministic geometry. Do not assume they supply authentic materials, handwriting, poses, or video rendering.
combinations: Works alone for diagrams and contour reveals. With style-001, use a modular grid and clear sans hierarchy; keep strokes tied to grid units and labels until paths finish. With style-024, add at most one loose handwritten note per narrated idea after the structure reads; keep it off endpoints. These are optional compatible combinations.
productionApproach: Select visual construction and motion tools for the style and action first; assign one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export pipeline. Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required output; record why. Keep renderer and motion responsibilities separate from export. For video, inspect representative and decoded frames, full playback, sync, dimensions, duration, frame rate, and loop continuity. For HTML, implement responsive and accessible interaction states.
